<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121640b94b83e1f97f8d6641d2632dcb55374b8f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `10d7de30ff57952439ef97be99f0b6ec904f104d` — the merge of head `ed69517ab066cd91ed02c669776c7bb6083420bb` into base `121640b94b83e1f97f8d6641d2632dcb55374b8f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 10d7de30ff57952439ef97be99f0b6ec904f104d && git checkout 10d7de30ff57952439ef97be99f0b6ec904f104d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 121640b94b83e1f97f8d6641d2632dcb55374b8f ed69517ab066cd91ed02c669776c7bb6083420bb && git checkout -B drift-repro 121640b94b83e1f97f8d6641d2632dcb55374b8f && git merge --no-ff ed69517ab066cd91ed02c669776c7bb6083420bb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121640b94b83e1f97f8d6641d2632dcb55374b8f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #32143 · head `6f8323af` · 2026-11-10T13:58Z

| Item | Reading |
|:--|:--|
| Shape | Draft, base `main`. First line `Fixes #32143`: one card, and no other card number sits beside a closing keyword (body scanned). Three files, +148/−0: `notify-node.ts`, `notify-delivery-outcome.integration.test.ts`, and a `@objectstack/service-automation` patch changeset. No governed path, under the 3000-line threshold, so this is not Tier H. |
| Premise, measured | The card's case reproduces on the PR's own pins: a push-only notify to an unregistered channel. The dispatch's decisive question was answered by reading `dag-traversal.ts`, not by assuming: `success: false` takes the fault edge or aborts. So the step stays `success` and carries the reason on `warnings`. The seat checked that this channel already exists on `main`: `warnings?: string[]` at `engine.ts:428` and `:1081` (origin/main). No new public field. `MessagingServiceSurface.deliveries` is a node-local structural mirror of what `emit()` already returns, so Clause-② stays `no`. |
| Gates (check-runs at `6f8323af`) | Green so far: Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size, Plan Test Core shards. In progress at review: Type Check ×4 and Test Core 1–8/8. ⛔ Not landed until every check is green or an expected skip. |
| Tests | Four new cases on the real `MessagingService`, outbox and dispatcher: durable path, inline path, a registered-channel CONTROL with no warning, and partial delivery naming only the refused channel. The dev reports an ablation that turned 3 of 8 red while the control stayed green, and a package run of 270 files / 3565 tests at `2386ad38` before merging main. No rejection case, so there is no `code`/`status` obligation. |
| Accepted deviations | (1) Partial delivery is warned on too. That goes beyond the card's "only channel refused" case, is declared in the body and pinned. (2) Repo-wide `pnpm lint` was not run locally. Changed-file eslint was run, and the CI lint lanes are the authority. (3) Three derived gates are NOT MEASURED locally (fixture commit outside the shallow clone, missing `dist/`, lock timeout). CI covers them. |
| Out of scope | A notify with no messaging service composed records `skipped` + success. It has no public-entry reproduction (stock deployments compose messaging), so it stays in Acceptance notes and is not filed. `Skills-docs:` not owed: `Metadata-protocol: none`, no narrowing arm. |
| Seat note | The warning passes each channel's own error text through verbatim into run history, which admins read. The same text already reaches the server log, so this is no new exposure class. The seat records it so a channel that puts secrets in its error text is fixed in that channel, not here. |
| Landing | Seat lands (not Tier H): once all checks are green, `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 32237`, then `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` in one relay call. The card closes through `Fixes` and its `pm:dispatched` is cleared at MERGED. |
